# stabilization/ - track-locked video stabilization toolkit

Stabilize a nadir/drone video so every tracked keypoint keeps its
FIRST-FRAME pixel position. Output is a fixed WxH window (optionally
offset in frame-0 coordinates). CPU-only, no GPU needed.

Pipeline: CoTracker3 tracks (.npz) -> camera motion.csv -> stabilized mp4.

## MANDATORY: verify parameters with the user BEFORE rendering

The tool enforces this mechanically. Do not bypass it.

1. Choose parameters (crop size, shift-x/y, frame range) from the video's
   resolution and the user's goal.
2. Run `plan` and paste the PROPOSED PARAMETERS block to the user VERBATIM:
       python3 stabilize.py plan --video V.mp4 --tracks-npz T.npz \
           --motion-csv motion.csv --out out.mp4 \
           [--crop 1024] [--shift-x 0] [--shift-y 0] [--frames 0] [--crf 20]
   The block includes crop window coords, border-safety check, runtime and
   size estimates.
3. Ask the user to approve or adjust. For videos longer than ~2 minutes,
   offer a preview first (`--frames 1200`) and let them check framing and
   stability before committing to the full render.
4. Only after EXPLICIT approval run `render` with the same arguments plus:
       --confirm "<what the user approved>"
   Without --confirm the tool exits with code 2 and renders nothing.

## Subcommands

- plan    validate inputs + print parameter block for the user (no output file)
- render  render stabilized video (requires --confirm)
- viz     regenerate the camera-motion sheet (trajectory.png style: XY path,
          per-frame translation, yaw, zoom scale, diagnostics, summary strip)
          from an existing motion.csv - instant, no RANSAC re-run:
      python3 stabilize.py viz --motion-csv motion.csv [--fps 23.976] \
          [--video-name DJI_0260.MP4] [--gsd m_per_px] [--out-png trajectory.png]

## Prerequisites per video

1. tracks .npz - keys: tracks (T,N,2) float32 ORIGINAL-pixel coords,
   visibility (T,N) bool, query_points (N,2), meta (JSON string with
   width/height/fps). Produce via COT3/ in this bucket; see REPRODUCE.md.
2. motion.csv - camera-convention per-frame similarity motion, produced by
   motion_from_tracks.py (same folder):
       python3 motion_from_tracks.py tracks.npz --out-dir out [--gsd m/px] \
           [--window 100]
   Grid points are re-defined every --window frames (default 100; windows
   0-99, 99-199, 199-299, ... sharing one anchor frame) because they
   diminish over a long context; the per-window motion is combined by
   chaining through the shared anchor frames. --window 0 = legacy single
   grid. Writes motion.csv + trajectory.png + printed summary (incl. a
   per-window table: anchor, grid size, mean usable, unreliable %).
   For FRESH grids per window, track per window (query grid at each
   anchor frame) and merge first:
       python3 merge_tracks.py chunk_0.npz chunk_1.npz ... --out merged.npz
   (chunks share anchor frames by default; see REPRODUCE.md). A
   single-query npz also works with --window, but the re-defined grid at
   each anchor is then limited to points still alive at that anchor.
3. stabilize.py plan / render as above. The renderer is agnostic to
   windowing: it chains the per-frame rows of motion.csv exactly as
   before; `plan` reports the windowing found in the CSV.

Dependencies: python3.10+, numpy, opencv-python-headless, pandas,
matplotlib (viz only), ffmpeg on PATH.

## Conventions (critical)

- motion.csv stores CAMERA motion; stabilize.py inverts to IMAGE motion
  internally: tx_img=-dx, ty_img=-dy, phi_img=-d_yaw_deg, s=scale.
- Cumulative forward map C_t maps frame-0 coords -> frame-t coords;
  output relation dst(u) = src_t(C_t (o+u)) is applied with
  cv2.warpAffine(..., flags=INTER_LINEAR|WARP_INVERSE_MAP). Dropping that
  flag produces garbage - do not "fix" it away.
- Border safety uses ABSOLUTE corners (origin+local) mapped through C_t.

## Known gotchas

- RANSAC is nondeterministic: motion.csv is the single source of truth;
  never re-fit transforms inside the renderer.
- Grid points diminish over long videos; keep --window (default 100) ON so
  the correspondence set is refreshed at every anchor. If a window anchor
  has few visible points, the per-window table printed by
  motion_from_tracks.py will show it (low grid_pts / mean_usable).
- Per-frame scale bias accumulates over long chains (~x0.992 det drift over
  7800 frames observed); keep crops well inside the sensor or smooth first.
- CoTracker pads windows: T = n_frames + 4; renderer caps at video length.
- npz meta needs allow_pickle=True when loading.

## Reference result

task_video-stabilize-full-2026-08-22T0544Z in z81980440/agent_bucket:
DJI_0260.MP4 (3840x2160@23.976, 7852 frames), crop 1024 shift-x 150 ->
residual keypoint drift <=6 px after 7851 frames, ~11 min render on 4 vCPU.
